claims.text: HEAs with sufficiently high concentrations of reactive elements such as Al or Cr develop a continuous protective oxide layer at high temperatures.
A homogeneous distribution of reactive elements promotes formation of an adherent protective oxide layer.
High mixing entropy promotes uniform dispersion of constituent elements.
Uniform element dispersion facilitates selective oxidation of reactive elements.
Reactive-element homogeneity at grain boundaries and within the matrix favors formation of a uniform oxide scale.
Al and Cr selectively oxidize at high temperatures to form Al2O3 or Cr2O3.
The selectively formed Al2O3 or Cr2O3 scale is continuous and adherent.
A continuous protective oxide impedes further ingress of oxidants.
High mixing entropy helps maintain a uniform alloy microstructure.
Reducing localized compositional inhomogeneity prevents disruption of oxide-scale continuity.
HEAs enriched in Al and/or Cr will form a thinner oxide layer than otherwise comparable HEAs with lower reactive-element content.
HEAs enriched in Al and/or Cr will form a more uniform and adherent oxide layer than the baseline alloys.
HEAs enriched in Al and/or Cr will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain than the baseline alloys.
Lower-reactive-element HEAs develop patchy or non-protective oxide layers under the same high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Patchy or non-protective oxide formation causes higher mass gain and more extensive oxidation.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply primarily at 900–1200 degrees Celsius in oxidizing atmospheres.
The behavior may not persist under reducing conditions or high mechanical stress.
The controlled test compares HEAs differing only in reactive-element concentration after exposure to air at 1000 degrees Celsius for 100 hours.
